activities.caption: pair each genre with the promise it makes
activities.name: nvPromiseMatch

config.prompt: The genre-literacy audit — pair each question with what it exposes:

pairs.left: is there a thesis argued from evidence?

config.why: Check the label first, then audit the verbs and adjectives — and when a piece mixes genres, the test is whether the shifts are signposted.

activities.anchor: Readers can audit a method; nobody can
activities.caption: file the sentence — checkable or needs a label?
activities.name: nvCheckBuckets

config.prompt: The classic test: every sentence of a news report should be checkable. File these:
buckets: needs to move or be labelled

items.label: a quote preserved in a recording
a sentence no one could check

config.why: A sentence no one could check is either analysis or opinion — it needs to move or be labelled.

activities.anchor: satire becomes misinformation only when the context is stripped
activities.caption: file the moves — may, or may not?
activities.name: vnMayBuckets

config.prompt: The label law: the more a format resembles news, the more explicit its label must be. File each:

items.label: sponsored content wearing the newsroom's typography
satire operating under a convention both sides know
a 60-second explainer on a reporter's own account

config.why: News is unmarked, analysis and opinion marked, sponsorship announced — on blurred formats the discipline travels with the journalist: say what you are doing inside the format itself.

activities.anchor: the fact of the criticism without endorsing it
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the neutral-voice audit
activities.name: nvVoiceSpot

config.prompt: One line of this news-report audit is wrong — click it:
lines: Verbs of happening, not of judging: 'the council voted'.
Numbers instead of intensifiers: 'a 40% fall', not 'a dramatic slump'.
Where judgement is genuinely in play, the reporter states it plainly: 'the deal was humiliating'.
config.correction: Judgement is attributed, not stated: 'opponents called the deal humiliating' reports the criticism without endorsing it.
config.why: The reporter's voice stays out of the sentence — evaluations belong to named sources, in their mouths.

activities.anchor: informative precisely because they are rare
activities.caption: bet first — the record and the other party
activities.name: nvMethodPredict

config.q: 'Unbiased news' cannot mean a reporter with no perspective — so what is the honest discipline?
choices: Method: verify before publishing, attribute what you were told, seek the other party's response, label evaluations visibly
Hiding every trace of selection decisions from the reader
Reporting only stories nobody could have an opinion about
config.why: Readers can audit a method; nobody can audit an invisible mind — choosing stories, sources and leads are editorial decisions, and the discipline is making the checking visible.

activities.anchor: the pass-through lag is typically months, not days
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the Bank of England worked example
activities.name: vnBoeCloze

config.text: The news: the Bank raised interest rates from 4.0% to %%0%% per cent. The analysis argues from evidence — the pass-through lag to mortgage rates runs in %%1%%, not days — and reaches a defensible conclusion about what the committee's attention has shifted to.
config.hint: The new rate, and the unit of the lag the analysis cites.
